source.title: Fairness Pruning: Locating Demographic Bias in GLU-MLP Layers via Differential Activations
source.authors: Pere Martra; Eugenio Martínez-Cámara; Alfonso Ureña López

record.tranche_reason: The study uses individual neurons as targets for its own demographic-bias localization and pruning method, but it does not test whether neuron poles have one or two interpretable jobs, evaluate explanation accuracy on held-out activations, or test the listed attribution-graph claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports differential-activation localization and neuron-zeroing outcomes on BBQ/EsBBQ. These bear on a broader question about neuron-level causal interventions, but the measured construct is demographic-bias response, not any of V1–V7 as stated. The zeroing outcomes are recorded below with versions ["none"]. The paper also reports capability-retention figures, which do not measure any listed version and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study ranks GLU-MLP neurons by unsigned differential activation on demographic prompt pairs and zeroes them to check causal relevance to BBQ/EsBBQ bias scores. It never labels neuron jobs, estimates interpretable shares, scores explanations, or builds attribution graphs. It also cites polysemanticity of individual neurons (Bricken et al.) without testing it. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that the bias signal is localized in the final layer of every model. They interpret the selected neurons as regulators within a redundant system rather than stereotype stores: zeroing the single top neuron (L15:166) barely changed BBQ.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses contrastive-prompt differential activations to rank demographic-sensitive GLU-MLP neurons and zeroes selected neurons; it does not use neuron-pole explanation or attribution-graph methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with model, demographic category, Top-K intervention size, and whether bias is measured in ambiguous or disambiguated context. The authors report category and language differences in other results.

fits_no_version.finding: Zeroing 1–40 neurons selected by unsigned BiasScore shifts BBQ bias scores non-monotonically and sometimes inverts the sign (Llama-3B Religion Top-20: disambiguated 3.84% to −1.67%). Capability retention averages 99.49%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Neurons selected by unsigned differential activation causally affect demographic-bias responses, but the direction of the change under zeroing is unpredictable.

fits_no_version.finding: Between 66% and 88% of each category's top candidate neurons are unique to that category. Per-category circuits are mostly separate, with a small shared set concentrated in the final layer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Demographic-category-sensitive MLP neurons in small Llama models are largely category-specific.

record.problems: The study tests only models under 4 billion parameters with SwiGLU MLPs, uses explicit-attribute BBQ/EsBBQ multiple-choice benchmarks, and limits interventions to at most 40 neurons. No quantitative uncertainty estimates are reported for the bias-score results. The authors also note tokenization-parity constraints, particularly for Spanish.
record.rows_left_out: Capability-retention benchmark values were not included because they do not measure any listed claim version. Spanish EsBBQ intervention results were stated in prose rather than a full result table and are not included as separate rows here.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or job shares.
No interpretability shares across models or scale. Models tested are 1–3B dense SwiGLU only.
No vision models and no test of the cat-and-car neuron or recursive generalization.
No comparison of interpretable-neuron share across architectures, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs and no comparison with replacement models.
No test of whether explanations from activating examples predict firing on new text.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: No rows bear on any version, so no verdicts are given. The category-overlap finding is tangentially related to neuron specialization but is not a job-share audit, so it is recorded under fits_no_version. Spanish EsBBQ results and the capability-retention figures are correctly declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Does not estimate the share of neuron poles with one main job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs.
Does not estimate interpretable-job shares across models or scale.
Does not test the InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or recursive generalization.
Does not estimate interpretability shares across architectures or test effects of tools, regularization, or capacity.
Does not build attribution graphs or compare them with trained replacement models or reconstruction error.
Does not test explanations against activation behavior on new examples.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

relation.reason: It relies on neuron-level functional specialization as the premise for its bias-localization tool and reports no result on any claim version.

tranche.reason: The study ranks GLU-MLP neurons by unsigned differential activation and zeroes them to localize demographic bias. It reports only its own method's effects on BBQ/EsBBQ and capability retention. It never measures neuron job shares, explanation accuracy or attribution graphs.

source_check.notes: All 20 sampled rows match Tables VII and VIII. No statement cites this study and no verdicts are listed. Models are base checkpoints (meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B, -3B); Table VIII calls them Llama-1B/Llama-3B and Table VII shortens RaceEthnicity to Race. Rows bear on no version (bias-score change, not neuron interpretability).
